chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so Ja'far ibn Hannan said to him, 'What do you say regarding al-'inah (buy-back) in a man who sells to a man, saying to him, 'I sell to you for ten, twelve (Persian) and for ten, eleven (Persian)'?' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is invalid, but he should say, 'I profit upon you regarding all the dirhams, such and such,' and he should bargain with him on this, so there is no problem with it.' And he (the narrator) said: 'I bargain with him and there are no goods with me?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.الْعِينَةِ: Buy-back or sale with profit margin, often used as a financial instrument

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on al-'inah when selling for immediate vs deferred payment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between a defective 'inah' structure and a valid one by emphasizing the necessity of explicit verbal declaration ('arbahu 'alayka') to avoid the ambiguity of riba in dual-price sales. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly focus on the precise wording of contracts to ensure that profit is tied to a genuine sale rather than merely a loan disguised as trade. The permissibility of stating 'I have no goods' further illustrates the flexibility within fiqh to validate the transaction's form while maintaining its substantive integrity.
